description: Crossy Road online free: hop a chicken across busy roads and rivers. Dodge the cars, ride the logs, grab the coins and see how far you can get.
lede: One chicken, one endless road. Hop forward across grass, dodge the cars streaming past on the road, then ride a log across the river — and do it again, and again, until the traffic finally wins. It starts gently, with slow cars and wide gaps, and the further you hop the faster and busier it gets. Your best distance is saved, so there is always one more row to beat.

p: Press Play and hop the chicken forward with the arrow keys, WASD, a swipe, or a tap around the chicken. Every hop moves one square: across grass, across the road, or onto a log in the river. Your score is the furthest row you reach, plus 5 points for every coin you pick up on the way.

The first three rows are safe grass, so you can learn the hop before anything moves. After that the world is a mix of grass, road and river, generated fresh every run, so no two crossings are ever the same.

sections.h: Roads, rivers and what kills you
p: On a road, cars and trucks stream past in one direction. Step into a lane at the wrong moment and you are squashed — so watch the gaps, hop between vehicles, and never linger in the middle of the road. Traffic gets faster and the gaps get smaller the further you travel.

On a river, the water itself is the danger: hop in without a log and you splash straight down. Logs drift along the river, and standing on one carries you with it, so hop across quickly and never ride a log off the edge of the screen. A tree on a grass row blocks your hop, so go around it.
Coins sit on some grass rows. Hop onto one to collect it for 5 bonus points — but only if the detour does not put you in front of a truck.

Hopping across traffic is one of the oldest ideas in arcade games: Frogger, released by Konami in 1981, had a frog crossing roads and rivers in exactly this way, and it became one of the most copied arcade games ever made.

Crossy Road, released in 2014 by the Australian studio Hipster Whale, took the same idea, swapped the frog for a chicken, made the crossing endless, and added coins to collect. It became a hit on phones, passed 100 million downloads, and turned 'why did the chicken cross the road?' into a game you can actually play. This version keeps the same rule: one hop at a time, and the traffic never stops.

ol: Hop in short bursts and pause on safe grass to read the road ahead. Rushing into traffic is the most common way to get squashed.
Time your hop so you land just behind a car, in the gap it leaves, rather than chasing the gap in front of it.
On rivers, hop onto a log near its middle and cross in two or three quick hops — a log carries you sideways the whole time you stand on it.
Coins are worth the detour early on, when traffic is slow. Later, the 5 points are rarely worth a risky sideways hop.
On a phone, swipe instead of tapping: a swipe always hops in the direction you meant, even if your finger lands off-centre.

p: If you like steering more than hopping, eat eggs and grow longer in the classic [[snake]]. For another endless run with jumps instead of hops, try the [[dino-runner]]. You can find every fast, fairground-style game in [[cat:arcade|arcade games]].

faq: Why did I die on the river?
The water is deadly unless you are standing on a log. Hop onto a log, cross in quick hops, and never ride a log off the edge of the screen — it carries you with it.
